summary: Daidō Moriyama is a Japanese photographer known for his black-and-white street photography and association with the avant-garde magazine Provoke. He has produced over 150 photobooks since 1968, and his work is characterized by a raw, grainy, and blurry aesthetic that challenges traditional notions of photography. He has received numerous accolades, including the Hasselblad Award in 2019.
